messages.content: Survey recent work on hydrostatic mass bias in galaxy clusters. Use the hydrodynamics emulator to predict CGD (gas density) and CTP (temperature) profiles at two redshifts and discuss how profile shape evolution affects mass reconstruction.

**Survey** — 34 tools on 3 servers, 6 read-only probes, 16 papers found.

Hydrostatic-equilibrium (HSE) masses come out systematically low. In simulations the bias (1-b) is about 0.8-0.9. FLAMINGO (2409.07849) finds a median b_HSE of about -0.1 for groups and -0.2 for clusters. At fixed true mass, HSE masses rise with redshift for groups and fall for clusters, and the scatter grows with redshift. The bias also depends on AGN and stellar feedback strength and on how well the analytic density and temperature profiles fit. Non-thermal motions (turbulence, bulk flows, rotation) and mergers are found to cause most of the bias: Nelson et al. (1306.3993, 1308.6589), Rasia/Lau-type merger studies (1112.3659, 2511.10730), and analytic non-thermal pressure models (1507.04338). Observationally, X-COP (1805.00035, 1805.00034) finds small non-thermal pressure fractions and HSE masses consistent with b of about 0.1-0.2 out to R200. Gas-fraction analyses of Planck-ESZ clusters (2204.12823) show a sample-dependent redshift trend in B that is degenerate with Omega_m, and the CMB plus cluster counts value of B about 0.6 remains in tension with B about 0.8. For the emulator part: HSE mass depends on the logarithmic slopes, M_HSE(<r) = -(k_B T r / G mu m_p)(dln n/dln r + dln T/dln r). So mass reconstruction is sensitive to how the shapes of the density (CGD) and temperature (CTP) profiles change with redshift, not just to their normalisations. In particular, profiles steepen in the outskirts and depart from self-similarity at high accretion rate (1411.5361, 1404.6250).

Quantities worth checking: Logarithmic slopes dln n_gas/dln r and dln T/dln r at 0.5 R500, R500 and R200 at both redshifts; HSE mass profile M_HSE(<r) from emulated n and T, with M_HSE,500c compared between the two redshifts; Relative change in M_HSE caused by shape change alone (profiles rescaled by E(z) and the self-similar T500 vs. full emulated profiles); Departure from self-similar scaling: n_gas/(rho_crit(z) f_b) and T/T500 against r/R500; Sensitivity of M_HSE to the analytic fitting form (e.g. Vikhlinin density, generalized temperature model) and to goodness of fit, following FLAMINGO; Response of profile slopes and M_HSE to feedback parameters (AGN, SN) at fixed halo mass.

**Plan** — 4 lines of investigation:
1. Use the HACC hydro emulator to predict CGD (gas density) and CTP (temperature) profiles for a fiducial cluster-mass halo at two redshifts (low, e.g. z=0, and high, e.g. z=1). From these profiles, derive the logarithmic slopes and the hydrostatic (HSE) mass profile, and quantify how the change in profile shape with redshift alters the reconstructed mass. — This is the core emulator deliverable. HSE mass depends on T(r) times the sum of the logarithmic slopes of n and T, so the shapes of the profiles, not only their normalisations, set the reconstructed mass. Comparing the two redshifts separates shape evolution from self-similar rescaling.
2. Test how robust the emulated profile shapes and the HSE mass are to feedback (AGN and SN) parameters and to halo mass, at the same two redshifts, and check whether the emulated profiles depart from self-similarity. — The brief and FLAMINGO report that the bias depends on feedback strength and on mass (groups versus clusters show opposite redshift trends). A single fiducial run cannot show whether the redshift trend in shape-driven mass bias is robust.
3. Produce a literature survey of recent results on hydrostatic mass bias, with verified quotes, so the emulator results can be placed in context: the size of the bias, its redshift and mass trends, non-thermal pressure, and observational constraints. — The task asks for a survey, and the emulator numbers need comparison benchmarks: FLAMINGO's b_HSE values, Nelson et al.'s comparison of fitted-profile and direct-gradient HSE masses, X-COP's non-thermal pressure fractions, the redshift evolution of SPT temperature profiles, and the B tension from Planck clusters.
4. Synthesis: apply the non-thermal pressure correction to the emulated HSE masses, and compare the corrected and uncorrected b_HSE and the scaled low-z profiles with FLAMINGO, X-COP and SPT benchmarks. — Two reproducible analyses in the brief are not assigned to any direction: the f_nth-corrected mass and the comparison with X-COP and SPT in scaled radius. Without them, the shape-evolution result is never tied to the literature benchmarks. (added by the critic)
Critic's view: revise — None of the listed tools does arbitrary arithmetic on arrays. The finite-difference slopes, M_HSE(<r), the E(z) rescaling and the error propagation would all be computed by hand from the printed arrays, so they cannot be checked. Fix this in one of two ways: (a) if predict_observable writes an output file, load it with load_table_data so the agent can quote the exact grid values used; or (b) report the radial grid points and the values used for each difference explicitly, so a reader can redo the arithmetic. Slopes from a coarse emulator grid are noisy, so state the grid spacing near each target radius.; Several definitions are assumed but not checked against the emulator. Confirm from describe_parameters and list_observables: (1) whether CGD and CTP are indexed by a halo-mass bin; (2) whether radius is given in r/R500, r/R200 or physical units; (3) whether CTP is mass-weighted or spectroscopic-like. If the profiles are stacks over a mass bin, 'emulator input M500 as M_true' is not well defined; use the bin centre and say so. R200 at 0.5-1x R500 extrapolation can fall outside the emulated radial range. Drop R200 if the grid does not reach it.; Two items are missing. First, the f_nth correction (a reproducible analysis in the brief) is defined in d-03 but never applied. Add a step that uses the d-03 f_nth formula, or add a placeholder for it, and note that d-01 depends on d-03. Second, the brief asks for sensitivity to the analytic fitting form (Vikhlinin density, generalized temperature model) and for Nelson's fitted-profile versus direct-gradient comparison. Nonlinear fitting is not possible with these tools. State this as out of scope, or at most compare a direct finite-difference slope with a smoothed or wider-baseline slope as a crude stand-in..

**Wave 1** — now exploring, in parallel: Use the HACC hydro emulator to predict CGD (gas density) and CTP (temperature) profiles for a fiducial cluster-mass halo at two redshifts (low, e.g. z=0, and high, e.g. z=1). From these profiles, derive the logarithmic slopes and the hydrostatic (HSE) mass profile, and quantify how the change in profile shape with redshift alters the reconstructed mass.; Test how robust the emulated profile shapes and the HSE mass are to feedback (AGN and SN) parameters and to halo mass, at the same two redshifts, and check whether the emulated profiles depart from self-similarity.; Produce a literature survey of recent results on hydrostatic mass bias, with verified quotes, so the emulator results can be placed in context: the size of the bias, its redshift and mass trends, non-thermal pressure, and observational constraints..

**Finding:** Nelson, Lau & Nagai 2014 (arXiv:1404.4636) give a redshift-universal non-thermal pressure fraction f_nth(r) = P_rand/P_tot = 1 - A{1 + exp[-((r/r200m)/B)^gamma]} with A = 0.452 +/- 0.001, B = 0.841 +/- 0.008, gamma = 1.628 +/- 0.019. The fit is accurate to about 10% over 0.1 <= r/r200m <= 1.5 and out to z = 1.5. It gives about 10% in the core rising to about 50% near r200m; there is no systematic mass dependence for M200m >= 6e14 Msun/h, and rapidly accreting clusters are 5-15% higher. The thermal-only HSE mass is corrected as M_tot = M_HSE,th + extra term from d(f_nth P_tot)/dr, i.e. P_tot = P_th/(1-f_nth). This is ready for d-01/d-04.

**Finding:** Benchmark table (verified quotes in references.bib). (1) FLAMINGO (2409.07849): median b_HSE = (M_HSE-M500c)/M500c of about -0.1 for groups and -0.2 for clusters; the scatter is smallest, about 0.1, at M500c ~ 1e14 Msun; at fixed true mass M_HSE rises with z for groups and falls for clusters, and the scatter grows; the bias is insensitive to the analytic profile form but sensitive to goodness of fit, and it depends on feedback. (2) X-COP (1805.00034): median f_nth about 6% at R500 and about 10% at R200; 1-b = 0.85 +/- 0.05 for Planck SZ masses; the B about 0.6 needed by CMB plus counts is excluded. (3) Wicker+22 (2204.12823): 3.8 sigma evidence for z-dependence of B with a Planck Omega_m prior; the result is sample-dependent and degenerate with Omega_m; B about 0.8. (4) SPT (1404.6250): clusters at 0.6<z<1.2 are about 40% cooler in the inner (r<0.1R500) and outer (r>R500) scaled temperature than clusters at 0.3<z<0.6; minimal pressure evolution outside the core. (5) Lau+13 (1306.3993): the summation and averaging (Euler/Jeans) bias methods are equivalent; the acceleration term is small inside but non-negligible in the outskirts of massive accreting clusters.

**Completed — Produce a literature survey of recent results on hydrostatic mass bias, with verified quotes, so the emulator results can be placed in context: the size of the bias, its redshift and mass trends, non-thermal pressure, and observational constraints..** Six papers are cited with validated verbatim quotes in /Users/nramachandra/hep-genesis-testing/projects/ramp-research-cluster-profiles/runs/261020_110147/references.bib: 2409.07849, 1306.3993, 1805.00034, 2204.12823, 1404.6250 and 1404.4636. Of these, only 1404.4636 was downloaded and read in full text (/Users/nramachandra/hep-genesis-testing/projects/ramp-research-cluster-profiles/runs/261020_110147/1404.4636.txt). The other five quotes and all benchmark values below come from abstracts retrieved with get_arxiv_metadata.

Non-thermal pressure correction for d-01/d-04 (finding f-001, Eq. 7 of Nelson, Lau & Nagai 2014, arXiv:1404.4636): f_nth(r) = P_rand/P_tot = 1 - A{1 + exp[-((r/r200m)/B)^gamma]}, with A = 0.452 +/- 0.001, B = 0.841 +/- 0.008 and gamma = 1.628 +/- 0.019. The fit is accurate to about 10% over 0.1-1.5 r200m and holds out to z = 1.5. It does not depend on redshift when radius is scaled by r200m; in r200c scaling it does depend strongly on redshift. The fraction is about 10% in the core and about 50% near r200m, with no clear mass dependence in the paper's sample (M200m >= 6e14 Msun/h at z = 0). Rapidly accreting clusters sit 5-15% higher. To apply it, take P_tot = P_th/(1 - f_nth) and use P_tot in the HSE equation.

Benchmark table (finding f-002):
- FLAMINGO (2409.07849): median b_HSE of about -0.1 for groups and -0.2 for clusters. The scatter is smallest, about 0.1, at M500c ~ 1e14 Msun. At fixed true mass, HSE masses rise with redshift for groups and fall for clusters, and the scatter grows with redshift. The bias does not depend on the choice of analytic profile form but does depend on how well the profiles fit, and on feedback strength.
- X-COP (1805.00034): median f_nth of about 6% at R500 and about 10% at R200. For Planck SZ masses, 1-b = 0.85 +/- 0.05. The B of about 0.6 required by CMB plus cluster counts is excluded.
- Wicker et al. 2022 (2204.12823): 3.8 sigma evidence that B depends on redshift when a Planck prior on Omega_m is assumed. The trend depends on the cluster sample and is degenerate with Omega_m; the amplitude is B of about 0.8.
- SPT (1404.6250): clusters at 0.6 < z < 1.2 are about 40% cooler than those at 0.3 < z < 0.6 in scaled temperature, both inside 0.1 R500 and beyond R500. Pressure profiles show little evolution outside the core.
- Lau et al. 2013 (1306.3993): the summation and averaging methods of computing the bias give the same result. The gas-acceleration term is small in the interior but non-negligible in the outskirts of massive, accreting clusters.

Not done because the tool budget ran out: no figures were extracted (so there are no figure numbers), the 2023-2025 search including 2511.10730 was not run, and 1805.00035, 1308.6589, 1411.5361 and 1507.04338 were not read or cited.

**Finding:** The HACC CGD and CTP emulators output scaled profiles, rho_gas/rho_crit(z) and T/T500, on 19 log-spaced bins in r/R500c from 0.0154 to 2.74. Both are trained only for z = 0 to 0.4987, so z=1 is unavailable and the high redshift used is z=0.4987. The halo mass bin and the T500 convention are not reported by the tool.

**Finding:** Finite-difference log slopes in ln-space (grid spacing 0.2878). At z=0: dln rho/dln r = -1.86, -2.54, -2.93 and dln T/dln r = -0.27, -0.58, -0.91 at r/R500 = 0.49, 1.0, 1.54. At z=0.4987: dln rho/dln r = -1.87, -2.74, -3.10 and dln T/dln r = -0.35, -0.51, -1.07. The 1-sigma uncertainty at R500 is about 0.10-0.16 on the density slope and 0.05-0.14 on the temperature slope.

**Finding:** The HSE mass is M_HSE(<x R500)/M500 = -(x t/2)(s_n + s_T), assuming kT500 = G mu m_p M500/(2 R500) and mu=0.59. With this, M_HSE/M500 = 0.41, 0.93+-0.05, 1.27 at z=0 and 0.38, 0.84+-0.05, 1.22 at z=0.4987, at r/R500 = 0.49, 1.0, 1.54. The implied b_HSE,500c is 0.075 at z=0 and 0.16 at z=0.4987. The convention-independent shape-only shift in M_HSE,500c from z=0 to z=0.4987 is -9.2% +- about 8%.

**Finding:** Comparison plots of the emulated profiles at z=0 and z=0.4987 (fiducial parameters) are in Figure 6 (CGD) and Figure 7 (CTP). Scaled density agrees within about 2% over 0.2-0.9 R500 but is about 13% lower at 1.5 R500 at z=0.4987. Scaled temperature is lower at z=0.4987 at all radii above 0.03 R500: by 12% at R500 and by 30% at 2.7 R500.

Inputs: the profiles are already scaled. CGD gives rho_gas/rho_crit(z) and CTP gives T/T500, on 19 log-spaced bins in r/R500c from 0.0154 to 2.74. Because the profiles are scaled, rescaling the z=0 profiles self-similarly to z=0.4987 leaves them unchanged, so any difference between the redshifts is shape evolution only.

- Density: within about 2% between redshifts over 0.2-0.9 R500, and 13% lower at z=0.4987 at 1.54 R500.
- Temperature: lower at z=0.4987 at all radii above 0.03 R500, by 12% at R500 and 30% at 2.7 R500.

Log slopes (z=0 / z=0.4987), from finite differences between neighbouring bins:

Hydrostatic mass: M_HSE(<x R500)/M500 = -(x t/2)(s_n + s_T), where t = T/T500 and s_n, s_T are the two slopes. This assumes kT500 = G mu m_p M500/(2 R500), with mu = 0.59, and takes the true mass to be the input M500.

| 0.49 | 0.41 | 0.38 |

The implied b_HSE,500c is 0.075 at z=0 and 0.16 at z=0.4987. These absolute values depend on the assumed T500 definition. The ratio between redshifts depends only on self-similar T500 scaling at fixed M500.

Shape-only shift: the -9.2% breaks down into the scaled temperature at R500 falling from 0.592 to 0.518 (-12.4%), partly offset by the slope sum steepening from -3.13 to -3.24 (+3.7%). The lower mass at higher redshift agrees in sign with FLAMINGO's finding that HSE masses fall with redshift for clusters (q-05). These are thermal-only hydrostatic masses with no non-thermal pressure included.

**Critic, wave 1** — continue: 5 findings stand up to the evidence, 4 questioned ('Nelson, Lau & Nagai 2014 (arXiv:1404.4636) give a redshift-universal non-thermal pressure ': The only full-text evidence (tc-261020_1-w1-d-03-34, chars 14000-26000) covers the simulation setup. It does not contain Eq. 7 or the fitted values A = 0.452, B = 0.841, gamma = 1.628. The excerpt also gives the sample selection as M500c >= 3e14 h^-1 Msun, while the claim says M200m >= 6e14 Msun/h; this was not reconciled. tc-41 only records a citation. The fit parameters must be shown from the chunk that contains Eq. 7 before d-04 uses them.; 'Finite-difference log slopes in ln-space (grid spacing 0.2878). At z=0: dln rho/dln r = -1': The slopes were computed by hand, not by a tool. The quoted CSV excerpts are cut off at r/R500 of about 0.09, so none of the bins used (0.49, 0.866, 1.155, 1.54) are visible. The values also disagree with f-008, which uses the same z=0 fiducial data: f-004 gives -1.86 and -0.27 at 0.49 R500, f-008 gives -1.98 and -0.31 at 0.5 R500.; 'The HSE mass is M_HSE(<x R500)/M500 = -(x t/2)(s_n + s_T), assuming kT500 = G mu m_p M500/': This rests on the unverified slopes in f-004 and on hand arithmetic. The +-0.05 error on M_HSE/M500 at R500 conflicts with f-008: there, the same z=0 quantity is 1.85 +- 0.3 in k_B T500 R500/(G mu m_p) units, which is +-0.15 in M500 units, three times larger. With the f-008 error, the -9.2% shift is below 0.5 sigma, not 1.2 sigma. The sign convention is also inconsistent. f-005 reports b_HSE as +0.075 and +0.16, but FLAMINGO defines b_HSE = (M_HSE - M)/M, which is negative. The comparison with the -0.1 to -0.2 benchmark needs a stated convention.; 'At z = 0 with fiducial parameters (kappa_w = 3, e_w = 0.6, M_seed = 1.3, v_kin = 0.65, eps': The values were computed by hand. The R500-adjacent bins (0.866 and 1.155) do not appear in the quoted excerpts. The 0.5 R500 slopes and the M_HSE uncertainty are inconsistent with f-004 and f-005, which use the same input files.).

Issues: The headline result is the shape-only -9.2% shift in M_HSE,500c, but its significance is not established. It comes from hand finite differences across two bins, and the same quantity carries an error of +-0.05 in f-005 but +-0.15 in f-008. The GP y_std at z=0.4987 is also several times larger than at z=0 in the excerpted inner bins (CGD std/mean about 0.68 versus 0.12), so the outskirt errors at z=0.4987 may be underestimated too. The calculation needs to be scripted, with uncertainties propagated from the GP, for example by sampling profiles within y_std or using the GP covariance if it is available.; The claim that CGD and CTP stop at z = 0.4987 is not visible in tc-21 or tc-20. Those excerpts show only the GSMF redshift list, which runs to z of about 1.75. This limit forces a departure from the task's two-redshift design, so the per-observable CGD/CTP redshift list should be quoted directly.; M_HSE at 1.54 R500 exceeds M500 (1.27 and 1.22), which is expected. However, R200c is not 1.5 R500 for every concentration, and no tool converts radii to r200m. The f_nth correction in d-04 needs r200m at each redshift, and r200m/R500c changes noticeably between z = 0 and 0.5 through Omega_m(z). This must be handled explicitly..

**Next steps after wave 1** — One wave and 10 tool calls remain, and no Python tool is available, so the plan focuses on what can be checked by tool. The open direction d-04 runs first. Its non-thermal correction depends on verifying Eq. 7 of 1404.4636 with a single read_arxiv_chunk call (about 2 calls). It must also handle the r/R500c to r/r200m conversion explicitly at each redshift, by hand, with concentration varied between 3 and 6. directions.goal: Use the HACC hydro emulator to predict CGD (gas density) and CTP (temperature) profiles for a fiducial cluster-mass halo at two redshifts (low, e.g. z=0, and high, e.g. z=1). From these profiles, derive the logarithmic slopes and the hydrostatic (HSE) mass profile, and quantify how the change in profile shape with redshift alters the reconstructed mass.
directions.rationale: This is the core emulator deliverable. HSE mass depends on T(r) times the sum of the logarithmic slopes of n and T, so the shapes of the profiles, not only their normalisations, set the reconstructed mass. Comparing the two redshifts separates shape evolution from self-similar rescaling.

# Shape evolution of emulated cluster gas profiles and its effect on hydrostatic mass bias, z = 0 to z = 0.5

## Abstract

We surveyed recent work on hydrostatic-equilibrium (HSE) mass bias in galaxy clusters. We then used the HACC hydrodynamics emulator to predict scaled gas-density (CGD) and temperature (CTP) profiles at z = 0 and z = 0.4987. The task asked for z = 1, but the emulator's CGD and CTP profiles only run to z = 0.4987.

Because the profiles are already scaled, any difference between the two redshifts is shape evolution alone. Using finite-difference slopes across the bins either side of R500, the thermal-only HSE mass at fixed true mass is:

| | z = 0 | z = 0.4987 |
|---|---|---|
| M_HSE,500c/M500 | 0.925 | 0.840 |
| b_HSE (FLAMINGO sign convention) | -0.075 | -0.160 |

The shape-only shift in M_HSE,500c is -9.2%. Its significance lies between 1.3 sigma and 4.3 sigma, depending on the unknown correlation of emulator errors between bins. The shift is driven by a 12.4% drop in scaled temperature at R500, partly offset by a 3.7% steepening of the slope sum. Its sign matches FLAMINGO's cluster-scale trend.

The redshift drop in scaled temperature is robust to the kinetic-AGN parameters. The resulting mass shift, however, is of the same size as the kinetic-AGN spread. A Nelson et al. non-thermal pressure correction overcorrects the masses, and its redshift dependence comes entirely from an assumed radius conversion.

All derived quantities were computed by hand from tool-returned emulator values, not by a script. The absolute bias values also depend on an unconfirmed T500 convention.

## Background

**Size and trends of the bias in simulations.** FLAMINGO (arXiv:2409.07849) defines b_HSE = (M_HSE,500c - M500c)/M500c. It finds a median b_HSE of about -0.1 for groups and about -0.2 for clusters. The scatter is smallest, about 0.1, at M500c ~ 1e14 Msun. The paper also states: "At a fixed true mass, the hydrostatic masses increase (decrease) with redshift on group (cluster) scales, and the scatter increases". The bias is insensitive to the analytic profile form but sensitive to goodness of fit and to feedback strength. The verbatim quote on the redshift trend is stored in the bibliography. The -0.1/-0.2 amplitudes come from the abstract and have no verbatim quote.

**Methods.** Lau, Nagai and Nelson (arXiv:1306.3993) show that the summation and averaging (Euler/Jeans) methods of computing the bias are equivalent. The gas-acceleration term is small in the interior but not negligible in the outskirts of massive, accreting clusters.

**Non-thermal pressure.** Nelson, Lau and Nagai (arXiv:1404.4636) is the only paper read in full text. It gives a redshift-universal fit for the non-thermal pressure fraction:

f_nth = P_rand/P_tot = 1 - A{1 + exp[-((r/r200m)/B)^gamma]}

- Parameters: A = 0.452 +/- 0.001, B = 0.841 +/- 0.008, gamma = 1.628 +/- 0.019.
- Accuracy: about 10% over 0.1-1.5 r200m, valid out to z = 1.5.
- Behaviour: f_nth is about 10% in the core and about 50% near r200m. There is no systematic mass dependence for M200m >= 6e14 Msun/h. Rapidly accreting clusters lie 5-15% higher.
- The redshift dependence seen with r200c scaling "has completely disappeared" when radius is scaled by r200m.

Other papers in the survey brief were not read and are cited here only as the brief's pointers: arXiv:1308.6589, arXiv:1112.3659, arXiv:2511.10730 and arXiv:1507.04338 on merger and non-thermal origins of the bias; arXiv:1411.5361 on accretion-driven steepening of outskirt slopes.

**Observations.**
- X-COP (arXiv:1805.00034, abstract only) finds median f_nth of about 6% at R500 and about 10% at R200, with 1-b = 0.85 +/- 0.05 for Planck SZ masses. It excludes the B of about 0.6 required by CMB plus cluster counts. Its verbatim quote is "We find that hydrostatic masses require little correction".
- Wicker et al. (arXiv:2204.12823) find 3.8 sigma evidence for a redshift-dependent B under a Planck Omega_m prior. The trend is sample-dependent and degenerate with Omega_m, and the amplitude is B of about 0.8.
- SPT (arXiv:1404.6250) finds that clusters at 0.6 < z < 1.2 are "slightly (~40%) cooler" in scaled temperature, both inside 0.1 R500 and beyond R500, than clusters at 0.3 < z < 0.6. Pressure evolves little outside the core.

## Results

### Emulator configuration

The CGD and CTP outputs are already scaled: rho_gas/rho_crit(z) and T/T500. They are given on 19 log-spaced bins in r/R500c from 0.0154 to 2.74, with log spacing dln r = 0.2878. Each bin has a GP mean and standard deviation (y_std).

The emulator has seven inputs:
- Five subgrid parameters, all described by the tool as AGN controls:
  - wind: kappa_w (2-4), e_w (0.2-1);
  - black-hole seed mass: M_seed (0.6-2, in units of 10^6 Msun);
  - kinetic feedback: v_kin (0.1-1.2, in units of 10^4 km/s), eps_kin (0.02-1.2, in units of 10).
- Two cosmology parameters: omega_m and sigma_8.

Halo mass is not an input. There is no separate stellar or SN feedback parameter. The tool reports neither the halo mass selection nor the T500 definition.

The fiducial run uses kappa_w = 3, e_w = 0.6, M_seed = 1.3, v_kin = 0.65, eps_kin = 0.61, omega_m = 0.1375 and sigma_8 = 0.8. One check could not be made: the critic noted that the tool excerpts shown display only the stellar mass function's redshift list, which extends to about z = 1.75. The z = 0.4987 ceiling for CGD and CTP is therefore not directly visible in the quoted output.

The prediction files are in `runs/261020_110147/` under the project directory, named `C{GD,TP}_z{0.0000,0.4987}_prediction.csv`.

### Profile comparison between redshifts

[[FIGURE 6]]

Figure 6 compares the fiducial scaled gas density at z = 0 and z = 0.4987. The two agree within about 2% over 0.2-0.9 R500. At 1.54 R500 the density is about 13% lower at z = 0.4987, so the outskirts are steeper at higher redshift.

[[FIGURE 7]]

Figure 7 compares the fiducial scaled temperature. It is lower at z = 0.4987 at all radii above 0.03 R500: by 12% at R500 and by 30% at 2.7 R500.

The GP uncertainty is much larger at z = 0.4987 in the inner density bins: y_std/mean is about 0.68 at z = 0.4987 against about 0.12 at z = 0 in the innermost bin.

### Logarithmic slopes and HSE mass

Slopes are finite differences in ln y versus ln r. The HSE mass is

M_HSE(<x R500)/M500 = -(x t/2)(s_n + s_T)

where t = T/T500 and s_n, s_T are the density and temperature slopes. This assumes kT500 = G mu m_p M500/(2 R500) with mu = 0.59, and it treats the density slope as the n slope (constant mu).

All four fiducial files were read in full. The numbers below were then recomputed by hand from those values.

| r/R500 | Bins used | z | dln rho/dln r | dln T/dln r | t | M_HSE/M500 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.487 | central, 0.365-0.649 | 0 | -1.863 | -0.271 | – | 0.408 |
| 0.487 | central, 0.365-0.649 | 0.4987 | -1.872 | -0.345 | – | 0.382 |
| 1.000 | 0.866-1.155 | 0 | -2.545 | -0.583 | 0.592 | 0.925 |
| 1.000 | 0.866-1.155 | 0.4987 | -2.738 | -0.505 | 0.518 | 0.840 |
| 1.54 (taken as R200) | central, 1.155-2.054 | 0 | -2.929 | -0.912 | 0.430 | 1.272 |
| 1.54 (taken as R200) | central, 1.155-2.054 | 0.4987 | -3.097 | -1.072 | 0.380 | 1.221 |

An earlier value of -1.98 for the density slope "at 0.5 R500" was a one-sided difference over the 0.487-0.649 pair. It therefore measures the slope at 0.562 R500. The 0.365-0.487 pair gives -1.745. With the bin pair stated, the discrepancy is resolved.

The density slope steepens with redshift at R500 and beyond. At R500 the temperature slope flattens with redshift, while at 1.54 R500 it steepens.

Treating 1.54 R500 as R200 assumes an NFW profile with concentration about 4.

### Implied bias, shape-only shift and error bracket

If the true mass is taken as M500, the uncorrected bias is b_HSE = -0.075 at z = 0 and -0.160 at z = 0.4987. These absolute values depend on the T500 convention. The ratio between redshifts depends only on self-similar T500 scaling at fixed M500, because the profiles are already scaled.

The shape-only change is M_HSE,500c(z = 0.4987)/M_HSE,500c(z = 0) - 1 = -9.2%. It breaks down as:
- the scaled temperature at R500 falls from 0.592 to 0.518 (-12.4%);
- the slope sum steepens from -3.128 to -3.243 (+3.7%).

The errors come from linear propagation of the GP y_std, bracketed two ways:

| Assumption about adjacent bins | M_HSE/M500, z = 0 | M_HSE/M500, z = 0.4987 | Error on the -9.2% shift | Significance |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Independent (upper bound) | 0.925 +/- 0.049 | 0.840 +/- 0.047 | +/- 7.0% | 1.3 sigma |
| Fully correlated (lower bound) | 0.925 +/- 0.010 | 0.840 +/- 0.018 | +/- 2.1% | 4.3 sigma |

Under the independent-bin assumption, the R500 slope errors are:
- z = 0: +/- 0.155 (density) and +/- 0.055 (temperature);
- z = 0.4987: +/- 0.100 and +/- 0.135.

The true GP covariance between bins is unknown, so the true significance lies inside this bracket.

An earlier error of +/- 0.15 M500 (+/- 0.3 in units of k_B T500 R500/(G mu m_p)) overstated the uncertainty. The independent-bin value is +/- 0.05 M500 (+/- 0.10 in those units).

### Kinetic-AGN feedback robustness

The CTP predictions were read at the kinetic-AGN extremes, with all other parameters at fiducial values:

| Variant | z | t(R500) | dln T/dln r |
|---|---|---|---|
| AGN-min (v_kin = 0.1, eps_kin = 0.02) | 0 | 0.565 | -0.617 |
| AGN-min | 0.4987 | 0.490 | -0.589 |
| AGN-max (v_kin = 1.2, eps_kin = 1.2) | 0 | 0.600 | -0.573 |
| AGN-max | 0.4987 | 0.526 | -0.621 |

At fixed redshift:
- The AGN spread in t(R500) is 6.0% at z = 0 and 7.1% at z = 0.4987. The GP y_std on t(R500) is about 1% at z = 0 and 2-3% at z = 0.4987, so this spread is about 4 sigma and about 2 sigma respectively.
- The spread in temperature slope is only 0.03-0.04, and its sign reverses between the two redshifts.

The redshift change in ln t(R500) is -0.144 for AGN-min and -0.132 for AGN-max, against -0.134 for the fiducial run. This is about twice the AGN spread at fixed redshift (0.060 and 0.071 in ln t). The scaled-temperature cooling with redshift is therefore robust to kinetic-AGN feedback.

The mass comparison is weaker. It was contested by the critic because the variant density profiles were not read: the density slope was held at the fiducial values of -2.54 (z = 0) and -2.74 (z = 0.4987) for both variants.
- On that basis, the shape-only shift in ln M_HSE,500c is -9.0% for AGN-min and -5.6% for AGN-max.
- The AGN-max minus AGN-min difference at fixed redshift is +4.6% at z = 0 and +8.1% at z = 0.4987.
- To first order, the M_HSE redshift shift is the same size as the kinetic-AGN spread and cannot be cleanly separated from it.

### Non-thermal pressure correction

The Nelson et al. (arXiv:1404.4636) f_nth was applied with P_tot = P_th/(1 - f_nth), giving

M_tot/M500 = (t/2)/(1-f) * [-(s_n+s_T) + dln(1-f)/dln r].

Converting R500c to r200m required assumptions not supplied by the emulator: an NFW profile with c200c = 4 and Omega_m = 0.3. These give R500c = 0.652 R200c and R200m/R500c = 2.60 at z = 0 and 1.94 at z = 0.4987.

| | z = 0 | z = 0.4987 |
|---|---|---|
| f_nth at R500 | 0.207 | 0.260 |
| dln(1-f)/dln r | -0.196 | -0.285 |
| M_tot/M500 | 1.093 | 1.035 |
| Corrected b_HSE | +0.09 | +0.035 |
| Correction factor M_tot/M_th | 1.18 | 1.23 |

The correction overshoots: the corrected masses exceed M500. The implied f_nth of 21-26% at R500 is well above the X-COP median of about 6%. The corrected redshift shift is -5.3%. If R200m/R500c is held at 2.60 at both redshifts, the shift stays at -9.2%. The redshift dependence of the correction therefore comes entirely from the assumed radius conversion.

## Discussion

The main result is that profile shape alone, at fixed scaled normalisation, lowers the thermal HSE mass at R500 by about 9% between z = 0 and z = 0.5. The effect enters mainly through the lower scaled temperature at R500, rather than through the logarithmic slopes. The slopes do steepen in the outskirts at higher redshift. This is qualitatively what arXiv:1411.5361 attributes to higher accretion rates, but here it only partly offsets the temperature drop.

**Agreement with FLAMINGO.** The emulated mass decreases with redshift, matching the sign of FLAMINGO's cluster-scale trend. The uncorrected z = 0.4987 bias of -0.16 is close to FLAMINGO's cluster median of about -0.2, and the z = 0 value of -0.075 is closer to its group value of about -0.1. The emulator's mass bin is unknown, however, so it cannot be placed on FLAMINGO's group or cluster scale. The absolute bias values also depend on the unconfirmed T500 convention. FLAMINGO's sensitivity to feedback is mirrored here: the kinetic-AGN spread in M_HSE is comparable to the redshift shift.

**Comparison with SPT.** The emulated cooling of 12% at R500 and 30% at 2.7 R500 points the same way as SPT's roughly 40% cooler high-redshift clusters. The redshift ranges do not overlap, so the comparison is only qualitative.

**Non-thermal correction.** Adding the Nelson f_nth moves the bias from negative to positive, which suggests the correction is too strong for this emulator. The critic noted two caveats:
- the Nelson sample is restricted to massive clusters (M200m >= 6e14 Msun/h) and uses a random-gas-motion definition;
- the fixed-concentration radius conversion ignores the decline of concentration with redshift and does not use the emulator's own cosmology.

An X-COP-calibrated f_nth (arXiv:2112.07554 or arXiv:1805.00034) should be tested before concluding that the correction overcorrects. The emulated profiles are thermal-only, so the uncorrected bias reflects shape effects and the mass convention, not non-thermal support.

**Dead ends.**
- Halo-mass dependence (groups versus clusters) cannot be tested, because mass is not an emulator input and the profiles are stacked in r/R500 for one fixed selection.
- The table loader failed on the CSV header row "x,y_mean,y_std" ("could not convert string 'x' to float64"). This forced plain-text reads and hand arithmetic.
- Citing the numerical benchmarks verbatim and comparing with X-COP profiles were blocked when the budget ran out. The bibliography has no verbatim quotes for FLAMINGO -0.1/-0.2, X-COP f_nth 6% and 1-b = 0.85, or the Planck B values. No X-COP profile values were ever quoted.

## Limitations

- **No scripted arithmetic.** Every slope, mass and error was computed by hand from tool-returned bin values. The critic also noted that the excerpts recorded in evidence stop at the 0.0866 R500 bin, so the outer-bin values used were read but are not reproduced in the quoted output.
- **Unknown bin covariance.** The GP covariance between bins is unknown, so the significance of the -9.2% shift is bracketed (1.3-4.3 sigma) rather than measured. A Monte Carlo would need a Python tool.
- **Unconfirmed emulator conventions.** The T500 definition, the temperature weighting and the halo mass selection were not confirmed. This affects all absolute b_HSE values.
- **Assumed radii.** R200 was taken as 1.54 R500, and the R200m/R500c conversion assumed c200c = 4 and Omega_m = 0.3.
- **Incomplete feedback test.**
  - The wind variants were generated but never read; they were the stand-in for SN feedback, which the emulator does not parametrise separately.
  - The kinetic-AGN density profiles were not read, so the AGN mass comparison holds the density slope fixed.
  - M_seed was not varied.
  - No feedback comparison plots were made.
- **No fit-based comparison.** No analytic-form fits (Vikhlinin density, generalized temperature model) and no fitted-versus-direct-gradient comparison were done. The tools cannot do nonlinear fitting.
- **Thin literature coverage.** Only arXiv:1404.4636 was read in full; the other five cited papers are abstract-only. The 2023-2025 search, including arXiv:2511.10730, was not run. arXiv:1805.00035, arXiv:1308.6589, arXiv:1411.5361 and arXiv:1507.04338 were not read. No paper figures were extracted.
- **Redshift range.** The high-redshift point is z = 0.4987, not z = 1.

## Open directions

1. Script the slope and HSE-mass calculation with Monte Carlo sampling of the GP profiles, or the GP covariance if available, to pin down the significance of the -9.2% shape-only shift.
2. Read the existing wind-variant and kinetic-AGN CGD files to complete the feedback test with real density slopes, and compare the feedback spread in M_HSE with the redshift shift at both redshifts.
3. Establish the emulator's T500 definition, temperature weighting and halo mass selection from the HACC emulator documentation, so that absolute b_HSE values can be compared with FLAMINGO's group and cluster medians.
4. Redo the non-thermal correction with a redshift-dependent concentration and the emulator cosmology, and compare it against an X-COP-calibrated f_nth (arXiv:2112.07554, arXiv:1805.00034).
5. Compare finite-difference slopes with slopes from analytic-profile fits or wider-baseline smoothed slopes, to test FLAMINGO's goodness-of-fit sensitivity and the method dependence in arXiv:1306.3993.
6. Read FLAMINGO in full text to verify the bias amplitudes and the redshift trend for the matching mass range, and add arXiv:2511.10730, arXiv:1411.5361 and arXiv:1805.00035 with verbatim quotes.

Title: Hydrostatic mass bias for galaxy groups and clusters in the FLAMINGO simulations
Authors: Joey Braspenning, Joop Schaye, Matthieu Schaller, Roi Kugel, Scott T. Kay
Year: 2024
Abstract: The masses of galaxy clusters are commonly measured from X-ray observations under the assumption of hydrostatic equilibrium (HSE). This technique is known to underestimate the true mass systematically. The fiducial FLAMINGO cosmological hydrodynamical simulation predicts the median hydrostatic mass bias to increase from $b_\text{HSE} \equiv (M_\text{HSE,500c}-M_\text{500c})/M_\text{500c} \approx -0.1$ to -0.2 when the true mass increases from group to cluster mass scales. However, the bias is nearly independent of the hydrostatic mass. The scatter at fixed true mass is minimum for $M_\text{500c}\sim 10^{14}~\text{M}_\odot$, where $σ(b_\text{HSE})\approx 0.1$, but increases rapidly towards lower and higher masses. At a fixed true mass, the hydrostatic masses increase (decrease) with redshift on group (cluster) scales, and the scatter increases. The bias is insensitive to the choice of analytic functions assumed to represent the density and temperature profiles, but it is sensitive to the goodness of fit, with poorer fits corresponding to a stronger median bias and a larger scatter. The bias is also sensitive to the strength of stellar and AGN feedback. Models predicting lower gas fractions yield more (less) biased masses for groups (clusters). The scatter in the bias at fixed true mass is due to differences in the pressure gradients rather than in the temperature at $R_\text{500c}$. The total kinetic energies within $r_\text{500c}$ in low- and high-mass clusters are sub- and super-virial, respectively, though all become sub-virial when external pressure is accounted for. Analyses of the terms in the virial and Euler equations suggest that non-thermal motions, including rotation, account for most of the hydrostatic mass bias. However, we find that the mass bias estimated from X-ray luminosity weighted profiles strongly overestimates the deviations from hydrostatic equilibrium.

arXiv ID: 2204.12823
Title: Constraining the mass and redshift evolution of the hydrostatic mass bias using the gas mass fraction in galaxy clusters
Authors: R. Wicker, M. Douspis, L. Salvati, N. Aghanim
Year: 2022
Abstract: The gas mass fraction in galaxy clusters is a convenient probe to use in cosmological studies, as it can help derive constraints on a collection of cosmological parameters. It is however subject to various effects from the baryonic physics inside galaxy clusters, which may bias the obtained cosmological constraints. Among different aspects of the baryonic physics, in this paper we focus on the impact of the hydrostatic equilibrium assumption. We analyse the hydrostatic mass bias $B$, constraining a possible mass and redshift evolution of this quantity and its impact on the cosmological constraints. To that end we consider cluster observations of the {\it Planck}-ESZ sample and evaluate the gas mass fraction using X-ray counterpart observations. We show a degeneracy between the redshift dependence of the bias and cosmological parameters. In particular we find a $3.8 σ$ evidence for a redshift dependence of the bias when assuming a {\it Planck} prior on $Ω_m$. On the other hand, assuming a constant mass bias would lead to the extreme large value of $Ω_m > 0.849$. We however show that our results are entirely dependent on the cluster sample we consider. In particular, the mass and redshift trends that we find for the lowest mass-redshift and highest mass-redshift clusters of our sample are not compatible. Nevertheless, in all the analyses we find a value for the amplitude of the bias that is consistent with $B \sim 0.8$, as expected from hydrodynamical simulations and local measurements, but still in tension with the low value of $B \sim 0.6$ derived from the combination of cosmic microwave background primary anisotropies with cluster number counts.

arXiv ID: 2409.07849
Title: Hydrostatic mass bias for galaxy groups and clusters in the FLAMINGO simulations
Authors: Joey Braspenning, Joop Schaye, Matthieu Schaller, Roi Kugel, Scott T. Kay
Year: 2024
Abstract: The masses of galaxy clusters are commonly measured from X-ray observations under the assumption of hydrostatic equilibrium (HSE). This technique is known to underestimate the true mass systematically. The fiducial FLAMINGO cosmological hydrodynamical simulation predicts the median hydrostatic mass bias to increase from $b_\text{HSE} \equiv (M_\text{HSE,500c}-M_\text{500c})/M_\text{500c} \approx -0.1$ to -0.2 when the true mass increases from group to cluster mass scales. However, the bias is nearly independent of the hydrostatic mass. The scatter at fixed true mass is minimum for $M_\text{500c}\sim 10^{14}~\text{M}_\odot$, where $σ(b_\text{HSE})\approx 0.1$, but increases rapidly towards lower and higher masses. At a fixed true mass, the hydrostatic masses increase (decrease) with redshift on group (cluster) scales, and the scatter increases. The bias is insensitive to the choice of analytic functions assumed to represent the density and temperature profiles, but it is sensitive to the goodness of fit, with poorer fits corresponding to a stronger median bias and a larger scatter. The bias is also sensitive to the strength of stellar and AGN feedback. Models predicting lower gas fractions yield more (less) biased masses for groups (clusters). The scatter in the bias at fixed true mass is due to differences in the pressure gradients rather than in the temperature at $R_\text{500c}$. The total kinetic energies within $r_\text{500c}$ in low- and high-mass clusters are sub- and super-virial, respectively, though all become sub-virial when external pressure is accounted for. Analyses of the terms in the virial and Euler equations suggest that non-thermal motions, including rotation, account for most of the hydrostatic mass bias. However, we find that the mass bias estimated from X-ray luminosity weighted profiles strongly overestimates the deviations from hydrostatic equilibrium.

Title: Constraining the mass and redshift evolution of the hydrostatic mass bias using the gas mass fraction in galaxy clusters
Authors: R. Wicker, M. Douspis, L. Salvati, N. Aghanim
Year: 2022
Abstract: The gas mass fraction in galaxy clusters is a convenient probe to use in cosmological studies, as it can help derive constraints on a collection of cosmological parameters. It is however subject to various effects from the baryonic physics inside galaxy clusters, which may bias the obtained cosmological constraints. Among different aspects of the baryonic physics, in this paper we focus on the impact of the hydrostatic equilibrium assumption. We analyse the hydrostatic mass bias $B$, constraining a possible mass and redshift evolution of this quantity and its impact on the cosmological constraints. We show a degeneracy between the redshift dependence of the bias and cosmological parameters. In particular we find a $3.8 σ$ evidence for a redshift dependence of the bias when assuming a {\it Planck} prior on $Ω_m$. On the other hand, assuming a constant mass bias would lead to the extreme large value of $Ω_m > 0.849$. We however show that our results are entirely dependent on the cluster sample we consider. In particular, the mass and redshift trends that we find for the lowest mass-redshift and highest mass-redshift clusters of our sample are not compatible. Nevertheless, in all the analyses we find a value for the amplitude of the bias that is consistent with $B \sim 0.8$, as expected from hydrodynamical simulations and local measurements, but still in tension with the low value of $B \sim 0.6$ derived from the combination of cosmic microwave background primary anisotropies with cluster number counts.
